reasons: Lake identity matches the asserted title, court, and year: Minnesota v. Dickerson, U.S. Supreme Court, 1993.
Lake citations match the asserted official citation, parallel citations, and vendor-neutral citation: 508 U.S. 366; 113 S. Ct. 2130; 124 L. Ed. 2d 334; 1993 U.S. LEXIS 4018.
The opinion states that officers may seize nonthreatening contraband detected during a Terry patdown so long as the search stays within Terry bounds.

The opinion gives the plain-feel formulation: if lawful patdown reveals an object whose contour or mass makes its identity immediately apparent, seizure of contraband is justified by plain-view-like considerations.
The case-specific limitation is supported: the officer identified the lump only after squeezing, sliding, and otherwise manipulating the pocket contents after knowing it was not a weapon.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum precision, add that immediate apparentness must amount to probable cause and that the frisk must remain within Terry's weapon-search bounds.

reasons: The opinion expressly analogizes tactile discovery to the plain-view doctrine and describes a plain-feel/plain-touch corollary to plain view.
The case refines plain-view logic by extending it to contraband discovered through touch during an otherwise lawful Terry search.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: The role could be even tighter as Key — Analogical Extension / Refinement, but the current role is supported.
